cards.when: a quarterly univariate series; dating peaks/troughs & phases (expansion/recession), NBER-style, without a model
cards.when_not: a non-quarterly frequency; you want probabilistic regimes (-> #30), a cyclical gap (the filters) or a multivariate cycle

alternatives.criterion: you want regime probabilities + endogenous transitions instead of deterministic dates; gaussian/lm only
you want a continuous cyclical gap instead of discrete turning points

alternatives.alt: state space / dynamic factor analysis (#58/#61, category 10)
alternatives.criterion: a latent common cycle from several series
monthly data (outside the surface of this card)

output_key_fields: states: ts of the regime, +1=expansion / -1=recession per quarter
peaks_index/troughs_index: index positions inside the series (not dates)
peaks_date/troughs_date: peaks/troughs as 'YYYYQn' labels
phases: data_frame type/start/end/duration/state/complete
avg_expansion_duration/avg_recession_duration: the mean duration over complete phases only
n_complete_phases: complete (non-censored) phases
the raw dating fit (a stub once serialised)
interpretation_traps: sign convention: +1=expansion, -1=recession — not the reverse, not a z-score
peaks/troughs are position indices, NOT dates; a peak = the end of an expansion/the start of a recession
the edge phases are censored (complete=False); they are excluded from the means — do not compare them with complete ones
an interior gap in average_over_phases is an error, not a silent omission; an entirely empty input is rejected
mincycle/minphase determine the number of turning points; the dating is not unique; mincycle>minphase (gate)
deterministic (v0.9.8, legacy/archived); no RNG

cards.method: Change-point detection in mean / variance / mean+variance (PELT/BinSeg/SegNeigh/AMOC)
cards.when: a univariate series; locating the POSITIONS of structural changes in the mean, the variance, or both (meanvar) with penalized exact/approximate segmentation; any frequency (not only quarterly)
cards.when_not: you want NBER-style expansion and recession phase dating (-> #88); probabilistic regimes (-> #30); breaks in regression coefficients with dates (-> #3); a continuous cyclical gap (the filters)

alternatives.criterion: you want cycle dating (peaks/troughs/phases) on a QUARTERLY series, not the positions of a structural break in the mean/variance
breaks in regression COEFFICIENTS (structural stability), not in the level's mean/variance
you want regime probabilities + endogenous transitions rather than deterministic break positions
mean: a level change; variance: a change in volatility (volatility regimes); meanvar: a simultaneous change in level & volatility

alternatives.alt: method PELT vs BinSeg vs SegNeigh vs AMOC
alternatives.criterion: PELT: exact, linear cost, an unknown number of breaks (default); BinSeg: approximate and fast up to Q; SegNeigh: exact but slow up to Q; AMOC: at most ONE break

output_key_fields: changepoints: 1-based SEGMENT-END INDICES (NOT the final n, NOT dates)
n_changepoints/n_segments: the number of breaks and of segments (=breaks+1)
segments: a frame of segment/start/end/length plus the per-segment parameter columns (mean, variance, scale, rate or lambda, depending on the test statistic)
segment_params/global_params: per-segment vs global (e.g. the Gamma shape, the assumed mean for a variance model) parameter estimates
penalty/method/test_stat/minseglen/Q/pen_value_used: the rules that produced the segmentation (an audit trail)
fit: the raw change-point fit (a stub once serialised; a register field for the changepoint_segments accessor node)
interpretation_traps: changepoints are SEGMENT-END INDICES (the last observation of a segment), 1-based; they do NOT include the final n; they are not dates

the parameter-estimate field names CHANGE with the test statistic: mean and variance for the normal; scale and shape for the gamma; rate for the exponential; lambda for the Poisson — do not always assume mean and variance
for a variance change point the mean is handled separately (estimated by ML, or supplied through know_mean/mu); it is a GLOBAL parameter, the assumed mean, not a per-segment one

the placement is STABLE even in the degenerate nseg==1 case (no change): the assumed common mean (variance/know_mean) and the Gamma 'shape' are ALWAYS in global_params, NEVER in segment_params/segments; per segment: mean(mean/meanvar)/variance/scale/rate/lambda
penalty='Manual' requires pen_value>0 (0 => no penalty => over-segmentation); 'None' segments at every point; 'Asymptotic' needs pen_value ∈ (0,1]
CSS/CUSUM (non-parametric) do NOT work with PELT — they require AMOC/BinSeg/SegNeigh (a hard gate)
BinSeg/SegNeigh: Q (the maximum number of breaks/segments) must satisfy Q < n/minseglen; AMOC finds at most 1 break

a matrix input is read as MANY datasets by the raw routine (a silent list rather than a change-point object); this node accepts univariate input only (gate); an interior gap is an error, since the spacing must be regular
deterministic — no RNG in AMOC/PELT/BinSeg/SegNeigh (verified with identical); no seed is needed
sources: Killick, Fearnhead & Eckley 2012 'Optimal detection of changepoints with a linear computational cost' (PELT) JASA 107(500) 1590-1598
Scott & Knott 1974 (Binary Segmentation) Biometrics 30(3) 507-512; Auger & Lawrence 1989 (Segment Neighbourhoods) Bull. Math. Biol. 51(1) 39-54
Zhang & Siegmund 2007 (MBIC) Biometrics 63 22-32; Hinkley 1970 (a change in mean) Biometrika 57 1-17

cards.method: Bayesian change point (the Barry-Hartigan Product-Partition Model, MCMC)
cards.when: a univariate sequential series; Bayesian detection of change points in the MEAN with a posterior probability of change at EVERY position (the Barry-Hartigan PPM, MCMC); you want soft/posterior probabilities & Bayesian model averaging rather than deterministic dates or a MAP segmentation
cards.when_not: you want NBER-style peaks and troughs with dated expansion and recession phases (-> #88); a change in variance or in the whole distribution, or multivariate data (-> #215/#213); a regression, panel or graph change point (scoped out); a length below 4 (a segfault gate)

alternatives.criterion: you want NBER-style peaks/troughs & dated phases (deterministic dates) rather than a posterior probability of a change in the mean
you want an exact MAP segmentation with a penalty (mean/var/meanvar), not Bayesian posterior averaging
a non-parametric change in the WHOLE distribution (not only the mean), multivariate
probabilistic regimes with endogenous transition probabilities rather than a partition/change point

output_key_fields: posterior_prob: an array of length n, the posterior probability of a change AT each position; the LAST element is blank, since the last position cannot host a change, and it serialises to null
posterior_mean: the smoothed posterior level per position (model-averaged, NOT constant within a block)
posterior_var: the posterior variance per position (finiteness/non-negativity gated; roundoff negatives ~-1e-14 → 0; genuine negatives < -1e-8 → a hard stop)
changepoint_index: the 1-based positions where posterior_prob exceeds the threshold (the final blank is excluded automatically)
changepoint_prob: the posterior probabilities at the detected positions; n_changepoints: the count
posterior_expected_blocks: the POST-BURN-IN mean(blocks[(burnin+1):(burnin+mcmc)]) — the expected number of segments (consistent with the other post-burn-in summaries; NOT the all-iteration mean)
threshold/p0/w0/burnin/mcmc/seed: the audit trail of the rules/parameters
bcp_fit: the raw fit (a stub once serialised)
interpretation_traps: the LAST posterior_prob is blank by construction — the last position cannot host a change, because there is no following block; do not read it as 0
a change AT position i ⇒ a block boundary AFTER i (the new segment starts at i+1); it is a position index, NOT a date
posterior_mean is NOT constant within a segment (it is a Bayesian average over partitions); no single 'best' partition is returned — that is deliberate (Barry-Hartigan)
STOCHASTIC (MCMC): the seed is mandatory for reproducibility; the same seed ⇒ an identical result, without reseeding two calls differ
the sampler accepts gaps and infinities SILENTLY and produces garbage (live-verified) -> a hard gate here
length(y) < 4 causes a SEGFAULT in the C core rcpp_bcpM (live-verified: n=2,3 crash) → a hard gate (>= 4)
p0 = the prior probability of a change (larger ⇒ more changes); w0 = the signal-to-noise prior; the detection depends on p0/w0 + the threshold — it is not unique
the p0 domain is (0,1] (a hard gate): p0=0 is REJECTED as a degenerate prior that structurally forbids any change (it would silently return zero change points for ANY series)
the regression, multivariate and graph cases are scoped out — this is a univariate mean change only
sources: Barry & Hartigan 1993 'A Bayesian Analysis for Change Point Problems' JASA 88(421) 309-319 [the Product-Partition Model]
Erdman & Emerson 2007, Journal of Statistical Software 23(3)
Wang & Emerson 2015 'Bayesian change point analysis of linear models on graphs' (the bcp >= 4.0 methods)

cards.method: Energy-statistics nonparametric multivariate change-point detection (E-divisive / E-agglomerative)
cards.when: a multivariate (n×d) series; detecting MULTIPLE change points in the distribution (mean/variance/higher moments) without a parametric assumption, based on the energy distance; divisive = permutation-test significance, agglo = penalized bottom-up merging
cards.when_not: univariate turning-point dating of peaks and troughs (-> #88); you want probabilistic regimes (-> #30); you want a cyclical gap (the filters, category 10); you want a structural break in regression coefficients (-> #3); a very small n, below twice min_size

alternatives.criterion: you want a data-driven number of change points with formal permutation-test significance (p-values per split); stochastic → seeded; the default choice
you have an initial segmentation (member) or you want a deterministic bottom-up procedure with a penalized goodness of fit; no permutation test; faster with initial groups
univariate quarterly data; you want peaks/troughs & expansion/recession phases (turning points), not distributional change points
you want regime probabilities + endogenous transitions rather than discrete change points; gaussian/lm only
a break in the coefficients of a linear model/regression, not in the distribution of the data

output_key_fields: changepoints: the interior change points (sorted; position p = a change BEFORE observation p, 2<=p<=n); WITHOUT the boundaries 1 & n+1

n_changepoints / n_segments: the number of changes and of segments (divisive: n_segments==k_hat, n_changepoints==k_hat-1); agglo: n_segments == n_changepoints+1 (CONTIGUOUS temporal segments, NOT length(unique(cluster)) — the cyclic clustering reuses labels)
cluster: an integer vector assigning a segment to each observation (of length n)
estimates_raw: the raw estimate vector WITH the boundaries (an audit trail)

p_values (the divisive route): one p-value per split, in the order the splits were found; the LAST is the terminating, non-significant split; n_significant counts those with p<=sig_lvl, boundary-inclusive, matching the stopping rule; WHEN a fixed k is supplied the p-values are all blank and n_significant is blank too, since no permutation runs

significance_tested (the divisive route): True only when k is left unset and a permutation test actually ran; False when a fixed k is supplied, in which case the permutation count is forced to zero internally and the p-values are placeholders, NOT evidence
gof_progression/gof_final (agglo): the penalized goodness of fit per merging step
alpha/sig_lvl/permutations/min_size/k/penalty: the rules that produced the result (an audit trail)
seed (divisive): the seed that was used (reproducibility)
interpretation_traps: the raw estimates INCLUDE the boundaries 1 and n+1 on the divisive route, and a cyclic wrap on the agglomerative one — those are NOT change points; the wrapper removes them, so report ONLY the changepoints field
the divisive route is STOCHASTIC (it permutes); WITHOUT a seed the p-values, and the borderline splits, change from call to call — the wrapper seeds the generator internally (default 20240101)
silently wrong: a gap or an infinity in X makes the routine return NO change point rather than an error; the wrapper fences it
silently wrong: twice min_size above the number of rows silently yields no change point; the wrapper requires at least twice min_size rows
silently wrong: the reference=0 (or non-positive) → it RUNS but the p-values are meaningless; the wrapper requires a positive integer the reference

the p-values are NOT aligned with the sorted change points; they follow the order the splits were found, with one extra terminating, non-significant split — use n_significant for the count that matters

silently wrong: the divisive route with a fixed k forces the permutation count to zero, so the placeholder p-values are all 0; do NOT read them as significance (significance_tested=False, and both p_values and n_significant are blank); only the data-driven route, with k unset, gives tested significance

silently wrong: the agglo clustering is CYCLIC → length(unique(cluster)) counts distinct distributions, NOT contiguous regimes (e.g. a symmetric mean 0→5→0 gives 2 clusters but 3 segments); use n_segments (=changepoints+1)
alpha is the moment index of the energy distance, in (0,2] with a default of 1 — NOT a significance level; do not confuse it with sig_lvl
the agglomerative route with penalty='none' can over-segment noisy data; 'num_cp' penalizes the count; the dating is NOT unique, since it depends on alpha, the membership and the penalty
sources: Matteson & James 2014 JASA 109(505):334-345 (a nonparametric approach for multiple change point analysis of multivariate data)
James & Matteson 2014 JSS 62(7):1-25 (nonparametric multiple change point analysis of multivariate data — the divisive and agglomerative algorithms)
Székely G.J., Rizzo M.L. (2005) 'Hierarchical clustering via joint between-within distances' J. Classification 22 151-183 [the energy distance basis]

cards.when: producing a probabilistic recession chronology from data rather than a committee's judgement, updated in real time
cards.when_not: you want the official chronology; the series is too short for regime parameters to be estimated

alternatives.criterion: a deterministic rule-based chronology
a probabilistic model-based date
several coincident series

output_key_fields: smoothed_probabilities: recession probability at each date
regimes: mean growth and variance per regime
peaks, troughs: dated turning points from a probability rule
expected_duration: mean regime length
interpretation_traps: THE RECESSION LABEL IS ASSIGNED BY THE USER, not the model: the algorithm finds two regimes and which is the recession must be decided by their estimated means
a probability threshold of 0.5 is a convention; the dated chronology moves with it
real-time probabilities are revised substantially as data arrive and are far less certain than the smoothed series suggests
sources: Chauvet & Piger 2008 (Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 26:42)

cards.method: Monthly Bry-Boschan dating with smoothing and cycle statistics
cards.when: the rule-based turning-point algorithm behind most published chronologies, with the censoring rules that make cycles meaningful
cards.when_not: the series is annual, where the censoring rules cannot apply; you want a probabilistic rather than deterministic chronology

alternatives.criterion: the standard deterministic rule
a probabilistic chronology
quarterly data with simplified rules

output_key_fields: peaks, troughs: the dated turning points
phases: expansion and contraction durations
amplitude, cumulation: depth and cumulative loss per phase
censoring: rules applied and turning points they removed
interpretation_traps: THE CENSORING RULES DO THE WORK: minimum phase and cycle durations are what stop the algorithm dating every wiggle, and changing them changes the chronology entirely
the algorithm cannot date turning points near the ends of the sample, so the most recent period is always provisional
smoothing before dating shifts turning points systematically, usually later
sources: Bry & Boschan 1971, Cyclical Analysis of Time Series (NBER)

cards.when: detecting a regime change as soon as possible after it happens, rather than dating it retrospectively
cards.when_not: the analysis is retrospective, where offline segmentation is more accurate; false alarms are unacceptable and the delay budget is unlimited

alternatives.criterion: retrospective, most accurate
classical sequential detection
you want a run-length posterior

output_key_fields: detections: dated alarms
run_length_posterior: probability over time since the last change
delay: detection delay against known changes, where available
false_alarm_rate: at the chosen threshold
interpretation_traps: THERE IS ALWAYS A TRADE-OFF BETWEEN DETECTION DELAY AND FALSE ALARMS; a detector reported without both numbers cannot be assessed
online detectors are far less accurate than offline segmentation on the same data, which is the price of not seeing the future
the hazard rate in Bayesian detection is a prior on change frequency and drives the alarm rate directly
sources: Adams & MacKay 2007, Bayesian online changepoint detection (arXiv:0710.3742)

cards.method: Multivariate and kernel change-point detection with penalty calibration
cards.when: the regime change is visible only jointly across several series, or in a feature of the distribution a mean-shift detector cannot see
cards.when_not: a single series carries the signal; the number of change points is known and the penalty is not needed

alternatives.criterion: changes are in the level
changes are in the distribution, not just the mean
the change is joint across series

output_key_fields: change_points: the detected segmentation
penalty: the value used and how it was calibrated
cost_path: cost against number of segments, for the elbow
segment_summaries: per-segment statistics
interpretation_traps: THE PENALTY DETERMINES THE NUMBER OF CHANGE POINTS, and calibrating it on the same data that is segmented is circular -- state the rule used
kernel methods detect distributional changes including variance and shape, which mean-shift detectors miss entirely
multivariate detection assumes the change is simultaneous across series; staggered changes are detected poorly
sources: Arlot, Celisse & Harchaoui 2019 (Journal of Machine Learning Research 20:1)

cards.when: finding repeated patterns and anomalies in a long series without specifying what to look for
cards.when_not: the series is short; the pattern length is unknown and results are very sensitive to it

alternatives.criterion: motif and discord discovery at a chosen window
you want regime boundaries, not patterns
you want periodicity, not motifs

output_key_fields: profile: the matrix profile and its index
motifs: the most repeated subsequences
discords: the most unusual subsequences
window: the subsequence length used
interpretation_traps: THE WINDOW LENGTH DETERMINES WHAT CAN BE FOUND: a motif shorter or longer than the window is invisible, and the results change completely with it
trivial matches -- a subsequence matching its own neighbour -- must be excluded or every point is its own motif
the matrix profile is scale sensitive unless the subsequences are normalised, which is the usual default and changes what counts as similar
sources: Yeh et al. 2016, Matrix profile I (ICDM 2016:1317-1322)
Zhu et al. 2016, Matrix profile II (ICDM 2016:739)

arguments.name: series
arguments.description: Handle to a univariate ts series of the same frequency as the dating.

arguments.name: dates
arguments.description: Handle to a BCDating object (from date_business_cycles register).

arguments.name: fit
arguments.description: Handle to an S4 'cpt' object (from detect_changepoints register field 'fit').

arguments.name: y
arguments.description: Handle to a QUARTERLY (frequency == 4) univariate ts series.

arguments.name: mincycle
arguments.description: Minimum full-cycle duration in quarters (default 5; > minphase).

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Optional name label of the dating.

arguments.name: y
arguments.description: Handle to a univariate numeric series (ts); without NA/Inf; length >= 4.

arguments.name: p0
arguments.description: Prior probability of a change U(0,p0) per position; ∈ (0,1] (default 0.2).

arguments.name: mcmc
arguments.description: Number of MCMC iterations after burnin (default 500).

arguments.name: x
arguments.description: Handle to a univariate numeric/ts series (without NA/Inf; not a matrix).

arguments.name: statistic
arguments.description: Which structure changes: mean (cpt.mean) / variance (cpt.var) / meanvar (cpt.meanvar). Default mean.

arguments.name: penalty
arguments.description: Penalty for selecting the number of change-points. Default MBIC. Manual/Asymptotic require pen_value.

arguments.name: pen_value
arguments.description: Penalty value: Manual => >0; Asymptotic => type-I error in (0,1]. A number only (not a formula).

arguments.name: method
arguments.description: Search algorithm. Default PELT (exact, fast). AMOC=at most 1 cp. CSS/CUSUM do NOT work with PELT.

arguments.name: Q
arguments.description: Maximum number of change-points (BinSeg) / segments (SegNeigh). Q < n/minseglen is required.

arguments.name: know_mean
arguments.description: ONLY statistic='variance': if True, the mean is considered known (mu).

arguments.name: mu
arguments.description: ONLY statistic='variance' with know_mean=True: the known value of the mean.

arguments.name: shape
arguments.description: ONLY statistic='meanvar' with test_stat='Gamma': the known shape parameter.

arguments.name: X
arguments.description: Handle to an n×d numeric matrix (multivariate series; without NA/Inf).

arguments.name: member
arguments.description: Optional initial segmentation vector of length the row count of X (default: each obs its own segment).

arguments.name: alpha
arguments.description: Moment index of the energy distance in (0,2] (default 1).

arguments.name: penalty
arguments.description: Penalized GOF penalty: 'none' (none, default) or 'num_cp' (penalty on the number of change points).

arguments.name: X
arguments.description: Handle to an n×d numeric matrix (multivariate series; without NA/Inf; nrow>=2*min.size).

arguments.name: sig_lvl
arguments.description: Significance level of the permutation test in the open interval (0,1) (default 0.05).

arguments.name: n_permutations
arguments.description: Number of permutations of the significance test (positive integer; default 199).

arguments.name: min_size
arguments.description: Minimum segment size (integer >=2; default 30; requires nrow>=2*min.size).

arguments.name: alpha
arguments.description: Moment index of the energy distance in (0,2] (default 1).

arguments.name: k
arguments.description: Optional: fixed requested number of change points (None=data-driven via permutation).

arguments.name: seed
arguments.description: Seed for reproducibility (e.divisive is stochastic; default 20240101).

arguments.name: seed
arguments.description: Seed for the random number generator.

arguments.name: seed
arguments.description: Seed for the random number generator.

arguments.name: hazard
arguments.description: Prior change hazard rate for the Bayesian detector.
